newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Warehouse reports improved first qtr sales.
newsitem.headline: Warehouse reports improved first qtr sales.

text.p: The Warehouse Group said on Tuesday unaudited sales for the first quarter of the 1996/97 financial year were NZ$128 million, up 17.5 percent from the previous corresponding quarter's sales of $109 million.
The directors said they were positive about sales for the second quarter and believed the company was well positioned to take advantage of the prime Christmas and summer trading season.
The directors said sales for the August, September, October months were uneven and inconsistent, with August up 18 percent, September up nine percent and October up 24 percent.
November had started very strongly with excellent sales over the Guy Fawkes period.
Two new stores were opened during the quarter, and five more were planned to open in the quarter to January 31.
Warehouse Stationery achieved unaudited sales for the three months to end-October of $5 million, a 23 percent increase over the same period last year.
The directors said they were comfortable with inventory levels going into the main Christmas and summer trading seasons.
Despite the increase in store numbers and retail square footage, improved inventory controls meant inventory levels were lower than last year's.
The directors expected benefits to flow from the introduction of AEG appliances into a further nine stores before Christmas.
The group will report second quarter sales, including December, in early February.
